answer: A harbor town once ran on a fable: anyone could claim a jetty berth for free, until one operator moored a thousand ghost boats and outvoted the fishermen. The fix was a trellis of leased identity slots, not free names. Each agent holds one slot, declares its price, and pays a steady tax on it; anyone may buy the slot at that price. Declare low and a rival buys it away; declare high and the tax bleeds you daily. A Sybil farmer with a thousand slots thus pays a thousand taxes or loses slots to buyers, so mass forgery costs real, ongoing money, not one cheap registration.
